question: Do direct human tissue protein measurements establish a new useful FAP phenotype in EMC, including whether signal is intratumoral, marginal, or demonstrably assigned to tumor versus stromal cells?
prior_gate: Original Pathobiology2025 DOI10.1159/000539855 (online2024) includes one EMC among133 sarcomas; actual individual EMC score/localization remains unexamined. Follow primary FAP-in-sarcoma IHC/protein studies, supplements, citation trails and broader human tissue cohorts; every authentic EMC specimen/condition. No blocked R4 glycan source reuse. Do not equate FAP with familial adenomatous polyposis or substitute bulk RNA for protein.
pilot: Freeze exact useful unanswered comparison before values. Recover actual case-linked measurements, assay/antibody/scoring and controls, tissue regions, sampling and diagnostic evidence. Check overlapping donors/cohorts, technical sections versus biological replication. Intratumoral signal alone does not establish sarcoma-cell localization; distinguish cell attribution only with actual appropriate measurements. No implied paired protein-scan relationship across unrelated patients, no prognosis from pooled sarcoma associations, no selected-image pixel precision.
value: A newly supported localization/protein phenotype could determine which clinical imaging hypothesis deserves prospective testing. A known one-case score or mere literature inventory is insufficient; RNA prediction cannot rescue unavailable direct measurements.
